## SECTION 0 — HOW TO READ THIS REPORT / EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Engine selected (Step 0-2..0-4):** Two-stage Free-Cash-Flow-to-Firm (FCFF) DCF with a 5-year explicit forecast (FY2026–FY2030) and Gordon-growth terminal value, discounted at a WACC I derive below. I chose FCFF over FCFE or a pure-multiple approach because (a) ROK carries meaningful financial debt ($3.2B) so debt holders must be paid before equity, and (b) the company's cash conversion is exceptional and the pack's filed OCF/FCF series gives me a reliable bridge to calibrate FCFF against. I cross-check with owner-earnings (OCF − SBC − capex) and with EV/EBITDA, P/E and P/FCF multiples.

**The one-line verdict:** At $437.08 the market is capitalizing ROK at **~33× forward adjusted EPS, ~22.5× EV/EBITDA, and ~33× free cash flow** — multiples that are only justified if you discount this cyclically-sensitive industrial at roughly **7% (i.e., a required equity return consistent with a beta of ~0.5)**. ROK's measured 5-year beta is **1.54** (confirmed by two independent sources), the 10-year Treasury is **4.69%**, and every CAPM-consistent discount rate I can defend puts fair value at **$162–$241**. Even an aggressively generous 8% WACC (beta ≈ 0.85) yields only ~$295, 33% below the current price.

- **Base-case intrinsic value: ≈ $188/share** (WACC 10.5%, terminal growth 3.0%).
- **Conservative (strict CAPM, beta 1.54, WACC 11.5%): ≈ $162/share.**
- **Defensible range across WACC 8%–11.5%: $162–$295.** Bull case ~$260, Bear ~$130.
- **Margin of safety at $437.08: −132% vs base** (price is ~2.3× my intrinsic value).
- **Final execution opinion: AVOID / UNDERWEIGHT. Do not buy at $437.** A value entry requires the price in the **$150–$240** range.

**Why this is not an error in my model:** To justify $437 with my growth path, revenue would need to compound at ~26%/yr through FY2031 at a 10.5% discount rate, or ~14%/yr even at a very generous 8% rate — both implausible for a mature industrial. Only a ~7% discount rate (≈ a "bond-proxy" treatment) makes the price work. The whole debate hinges on the discount rate, so I show the full WACC sensitivity explicitly rather than picking one silently (framework requirement).
